w: Swamishri performed the ground-breaking ceremony of Lake University and addressed the students of Lake Primary School.
At 10.25am, Swamishri performed the Bhumi pujan of the new mandir to be constructed in Tampa.

In the evening assembly, the acting Mayor of Tampa, Mr. Charlie Miranda, presented a 'Key to the City' to Swamishri. He lauded Swamishri's work during his brief address. Lord Harikrishna Maharaj was honored with devotion by the devotees of Tampa.
At 10.45 am, Swamishri arrived at Jivaraj Park, Amdavad. Swamishri performed the murti-pratishtha of Akshar Purushottam Maharaj and Guru Parampara at the newly constructed 'Swaminarayan Sanskardham.'
At 5.10 p.m., Swamishri got news of the terrorist attack in Akshardham monument, Gandhinagar. (For details see special report).

Jal Jhilani Festival In the morning Kenya’s Minister for Special Programmes, James Carroom, attended a special assembly in which Swamishri donated grains to the government on behalf of the BAPS to help in their famine relief programme.

At 11.00 am Swamishri arrived at the Visa Oswal Sports Complex for the Jal-Jhilani celebration. Over 500 devotees attended the festival held in the swimming pool arena. Blessing the assembly, Swamishri said, “Life is an ocean. Just as a person drowns in the ocean, so it happens in life. If a person is (spiritually) ignorant, he will drown even in a small puddle. So, if we have the refuge of God, we can swim across.”

ds.t: Seeing one's nature as an enemy
w: A spiritual seeker said, "My nature is a hindrance to me."
Pramukh Swami Maharaj said, "How much it hurts us when someone troubles us! Do we feel the same hurt when our nature troubles us? If we regard our nature as an enemy, it will go from within."
Karsanbhai, who had come from Surat, said, "In Bhadra we get everyone to give up their addictions, but then people slip back into them again."
Pramukh Swami Maharaj said, "Let them. We should keep insisting that they give up addictions, explain to them and be patient. Little by little they will give them up."
Pramukh Swami Maharaj was having his meal. Meanwhile the sadhus spoke about their travels in the month of Shravan.
Hearing this report, Swamishri said, "The sadhus take great trouble and work very hard."
Paramvivek Swami said, "We cannot work as hard as you have worked. Whatever task you take in hand, you always complete it. We become lazy. You never get tired at all."
Gnanvijay Swami said, "Doing things without interest is very hard."
Paramvivek Swami said, "At 90 you still do not get tired at all."

Swamishri said, "It goes on by the grace of Shriji Maharaj. As long as the body keeps going, let us do as much seva as we can. We sing, don't we, 'May my life leave me while I am doing devotion....'" (Swamishri sang this line twice.)

Swamishri continued, "Those before us (Shastriji Maharaj and Yogiji Maharaj) did a great deal. So if we too do the same, God will be pleased, won't he! However much we can do, in whatever way we can, we should do it to please God."
Narayancharan Swami said, "We have only one hardship left now. At mealtimes the body has to bear great hardship (because of so much food); otherwise, where is there any hardship now?"

Swamishri said, "Our forefathers earned it for us. They did austerity, renunciation and hard work, and ate rotlas they had begged for. Now, because of their merit, we get 'plenty and more'. It is their merit, so enjoy the comfort. Be happy with whatever facilities there are at the time. When sometimes we do not get things, we should not feel unhappy and think, 'Nothing is in order here, let us leave.' Do not even think such a thought."
Vedantpriya Swami said, "Compared with the way you went to the villages enduring hardship, we have no hardship at all."

Swamishri said, "Those were the times then, and these are the times now, but what matters is that it is done with an understanding of glory. What matters is that it is done with enthusiasm and joy. All the sadhus have just been to the villages and the reports are coming in. There were very good katha sessions and padharamanis (visits to devotees' homes). Whatever the comforts or discomforts, everyone did the padharamanis. Because there is an understanding of glory, nothing becomes a problem. If we remember that our gurus did the same, then no hardship will be felt."

ds.t: Treat your nature as an enemy
w: A seeker said, "My nature troubles me."
Pramukh Swami Maharaj said, "How much pain do we feel when someone troubles us? Do we feel pain like that when our nature troubles us? If we regard our nature as an enemy, it will go from within."
Karsanbhai, who had come from Surat, said, "In Bhadra we get everyone to give up their addictions, but people fall back into their addictions again."
Pramukh Swami Maharaj said, "Let them do so. We should keep insisting that they give up addictions, explain to them and be patient. In this way they will give them up."

ds.t: As long as the body runs
w: Pramukh Swami Maharaj was having his meal. Meanwhile, the sants spoke about their travels during the month of Shravan.
Hearing this report, Swamishri said, "The sants take great pains and work very hard."
Paramvivek Swami said, "We cannot work as hard as you have. Whatever task you take in hand, you complete it. We become lazy. You never get tired at all."
Gnanvijay Swami said, "Doing it without interest is very difficult."
Paramvivek Swami said, "Even at 90 you do not get tired at all."

Swamishri said, "It goes on by the grace of Shriji Maharaj. As long as the body runs, let us do as much seva as we can. We sing, don't we, 'May my life leave me while I am doing devotion...'" (Swamishri sang this line twice.)

Then Swamishri said, "Those before us (Shastriji Maharaj and Yogiji Maharaj) did a great deal. So if we too do it the same way, Bhagwan will be pleased, won't he! As much as we can, however we can, we should do it to please Bhagwan."
Narayancharan Swami said, "Now we have only one hardship left. At mealtimes the body suffers a lot of hardship, otherwise where is there any hardship now?"

Swamishri said, "Our forefathers earned it all. They did austerity, renunciation and hard work, and ate bread they had begged for. Now, by their merit, we get everything ready made. Since it is their merit, enjoy the comfort. Be happy with whatever facilities there are at the time. If sometimes we do not get them, we should not be upset and think, 'There is no proper arrangement here at all, let us leave.' Do not even think that."
Vedantpriya Swami said, "Compared with the hardships you bore going to the villages, we have no hardship at all."

Swamishri said, "The times were like that then, and the times are like this now, but what matters is that it is done with an understanding of the glory. What matters is that it is done with enthusiasm and joy. Reports are coming in now of all the sants who went to the villages. There were very good katha sessions and padhramanis (visits to devotees' homes). Whether it was convenient or not, everyone did padhramanis. Because there is understanding of the glory, there is no problem. If we remember that our gurus did the same, there will be no hardship at all."

Today was Mahant Swami Maharaj's birthday according to the Indian calendar. Swamishri had instructed the organising sadhus well beforehand that it should be celebrated simply, and that in the morning puja and the birthday assembly only kirtans and discourses about Swamibapa should be held. Through this he had registered in advance his devotion at the feet of his guru, Pramukh Swami Maharaj.

When Swamishri, so bowed down with the weight of devotion, came out of his room on the morning of his birthday, the sadhus were standing before him, eager to receive his first glance of the day. As soon as they had Swamishri's darshan, everyone bowed their heads. At that time, instead of placing his hand on everyone's head and blessing them, words slipped from Swamishri's lips: "Please bless me..."
With this darshan of Swamishri, like "humble, behaving without claims...", the dawning morning was coloured!

ds.t: First to arrive at the camp
w: Since the morning, the "Akshar Purushottam Darshan" camp had been held in the mandir.
In connection with it, when Mahant Swami Maharaj woke in the afternoon, the first thing he said was, "I want to go to the camp."

By Swamishri's wish, the Akshar Purushottam camp had begun in the morning itself. After the afternoon break, the camp was due to restart at 4.00, but Swamishri was the very first to arrive, going and taking his seat in the camp at 3.55. All the devotees (some in the assembly hall too) were still resting. Even the speaker had not come. But Swamishri had arrived...!!

By coincidence, Bhadreshdas Swami had gone there to see what the atmosphere was like, and on seeing Swamishri, so that Swamishri's time would not be wasted, he sat down to give his talk right then, though it was scheduled for later.
Such enthusiasm, in the very manifest form of Akshar Purushottam, to listen to talks about Akshar Purushottam!!
At the end of the camp, Mahant Swami Maharaj asked for the microphone and, showering his third blessings of the day, said:
"Let us speak of the glory of the children sitting here... Children, stand up." All the children immediately stood up. Swamishri said, "Sit down." They all sat down again.

Then Swamishri said, "We go to the seashore, and millions of people go, because there is ozone there, which is good for health. It improves health, but many do not know that. In the same way, these children do not know what is happening here. But this is knowledge with a seed in it; it will reach right into the heart. Just as ozone does its work, so this knowledge will also do its work. There is not the slightest doubt about it."

From the time Swamishri went and sat in the camp at 3.55 until 7.30 in the evening, he sat for 215 minutes without a break as the very best listener. He did not even get up to pass urine. He did not cross one leg over the other. He did not even drink water. And there was no question of dozing or boredom. Constantly turning his mala, he listened to every single word with complete attention and interest!

The words Shriji Maharaj used for himself in Vachanamrut Gadhada II 49, "As for me, my mind is never satiated by the katha, kirtan and talks of Bhagwan or by meditation on Bhagwan," were seen in Swamishri.
Mahant Swami Maharaj sang the chesta. Then, after his bath, he came to rest. Swamishri looked at the clock. It was 9.55. The sadhus asked, "Are you feeling fresh?"
Sitting for so long without a break, and listening attentively the whole time, is bound to be tiring, as everyone had felt. That is why they asked Swamishri this question.
But Swamishri is a person made of a different clay altogether! So he said with a smile full of joy, "We are quite fresh!"

The sadhus said, "But Swami! You did not move even slightly. You did not even cross one leg over the other. And there was no question of dozing off. You sat completely still, turning your mala (rosary) and listening to the katha (spiritual discourse), listening and listening. You broke the record!"
Swamishri said, full of the glory of it, "Where else would we get to hear such first class talks?"
Bhadreshdas Swami asked with curiosity, "How long could you listen, Swami?"
Swamishri laughed and said, "Another two or two and a half hours."
The sadhus said in wonder and awe, "Swami! You have already sat for seven and a half hours in total, and another two or two and a half hours?!"

Swamishri laughed and said, "We were in a village once. It was Nom (the ninth day of the lunar fortnight, a fast day), so there was no meal! We sat from 6 in the morning until 12 at night without a break."
"Oh!" escaped from the sadhus' mouths, and they asked, "Which village was it, Swami?"
Swamishri said, "The village of Ramanbhai Sheth's brother in law (Bamaniya)."
The sadhus' curiosity kept growing. They asked, "Who was giving the katha?"
Swamishri said, "There was just Vallabhbhai and two or three others."
The sadhus asked, "And you were listening?"
Swamishri said, "No, we were discussing among ourselves."
"Then Swami! What year would it have been?"
Swamishri said, "1982!"
The sadhus could not contain their amazement. Once again they asked, "Swami! From 6 in the morning until 12 at night, you sat for eighteen hours straight!!"
Swamishri laughed and nodded yes, saying, "Yes, we sat down after puja. We did not even notice the time!"

The sadhus laughed in astonishment. It was truly amazing! Talking and listening to katha for eighteen hours straight, and still not even noticing! Swamishri had held a discussion worthy of a place in the Guinness Book of World Records.
Bhadreshdas Swami said, "Swami! In so many hours, however much material there might be, it would all get finished."
Digantbhai Sadhak asked, "Swami! What were you discussing?"

Swamishri said, "The first two volumes of the Haricharitramrut Sagar." Then Swamishri said, "I still remember one thing from the first volume: 'Honour and insult are all perishable, so one should not be affected by them.'"

The epithet Shri Achintyanand Varni used for Gunatitanand Swami, "Paramharivartavyasaninam" (one who is supremely devoted to talks about Bhagwan), fully applies to Swamishri, the manifest Gunatit, as well.
